problems.name: Integer multiplication
problems.assumptions: Two n-bit integers, exact output, deterministic worst-case time on one fixed finite-alphabet machine with finitely many one-dimensional tapes. Constants and machine are fixed before inputs vary.
problems.formalizationScope: The catalogue does not list an accompanying top-line Lean formalization for this multiplication claim.

problems.name: Fourier transforms
problems.assumptions: Every positive transform length, exact complex arithmetic, unrestricted coefficients, and a supplied root of unity. Scalar preparation and logarithmic-word indexing are counted; finite-precision stability and bit complexity are different questions.
problems.formalizationScope: The upstream notes report a uniform all-length 10⁻¹³ theorem and a separate subsequential circuit theorem. The latter alone would not imply an all-length algorithm; extraction/search uniformization is outside the selected statements.

problems.name: Matrix multiplication
problems.assumptions: Square matrix multiplication over ℂ in division-free arithmetic programs, allowing every fixed positive exponent slack ε. This is an arithmetic-operation bound, not a bit-operation or benchmark bound.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes report ω(ℂ) ≤ 9/4, plus separate rectangular and all-field bounds. Their all-field result is < 2.371054886006746; it does not by itself establish 9/4 over every field.

problems.name: Zero-free regions
problems.assumptions: The strict half-plane Re(s) > β for Dirichlet L-functions and finite-order Hecke L-functions over ℚ(√−3). Principal-character poles at s = 1 are excluded. No claim is made about the boundary line.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes report 7/8 bounds for zeta, Dirichlet, and the specified Hecke functions. This dashboard has not compiled or audited their theorem dependencies.

problems.name: Heilbronn triangles
problems.assumptions: The manuscript claim concerns n points in the unit square and all sufficiently large n, with one fixed positive area-exponent saving. It is an asymptotic construction, not a finite point-set record.
problems.formalizationScope: The reported Lean statement covers an unbounded sequence of sizes. The manuscript’s every-sufficiently-large-n claim is broader; the existence of the linked formalization does not certify that broader scope.

problems.name: Job scheduling
problems.assumptions: Nonpreemptive unit-length jobs with arbitrary acyclic precedence constraints on three identical parallel machines. The objective is minimum makespan, and the input explicitly encodes the precedence graph.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes report exact deadline feasibility and optimal schedules for nonempty instances in polynomial binary-input time. Four-machine adaptations require their own completeness and optimality arguments.

problems.name: Subset Sum
problems.assumptions: Worst-case lists of positive integers, including repeats, with polynomial-bit inputs. Randomized word-RAM time is bounded on every execution; success is at least 2/3 per input, with O(n+b)-bit words.
problems.formalizationScope: The catalogue does not list an accompanying top-line Lean formalization for this Subset Sum claim.

problems.name: Time-to-space simulation
problems.assumptions: A fixed deterministic machine with one writable tape and finitely many read-only input heads; head moves are local, initial contents are independent of T, and symbols have polylogarithmic-space access. Simulation time is unrestricted.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes report finite-control and halting outcomes in two-fifths-power space. General multitape simulations and hierarchy consequences are outside the selected statements.

problems.name: Permanent lower bounds
problems.assumptions: The complex n×n permanent, represented by determinants of affine-linear matrices or coefficientwise limits of such representations. The lower bound holds asymptotically for matrix size.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes report cubic exact and border determinantal lower bounds, including an explicit threshold. Broader algebraic-branching-program consequences are outside those statements.

problems.name: Strategy games
problems.assumptions: The manuscript’s deterministic quasipolynomial bit-time claim uses complete binary input length L, including signed rewards, rational probabilities, and priorities. Its ordinary, stochastic, and parity variants have distinct output guarantees.
problems.formalizationScope: The reported Lean scope is a randomized ordinary mean-payoff winning-set algorithm with success ≥ 7/8, plus a finite counterexample. It does not certify the deterministic and extended-game claims shown in the family description.

problems.name: Exact graph matching
problems.assumptions: Simple undirected graphs, exact maximum-cardinality matching, randomized word time, and success at least 2/3. The time bound holds on every computation path.
problems.formalizationScope: The catalogue does not list an accompanying top-line Lean formalization for this matching claim.

problems.name: Edit distance
problems.assumptions: Unit-cost edit distance, fixed rational relative error ε ∈ (0,1), total length N, and polynomially bounded integer symbols. The approximation succeeds with probability at least 2/3; the time guarantee is expected time.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes report a randomized (1+ε) estimate in expected almost-linear work at fixed accuracy. This is not an exact-distance or deterministic worst-case-time claim.

problems.name: Deletion-trace reconstruction
problems.assumptions: Worst-case binary strings, independent deletion traces, and a fixed deletion probability in (0,1). Upper and lower sample bounds answer different questions; the uniform decoder upper bound assumes a known fixed rational retention probability.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes report superpolynomial and quantitative sample lower bounds. The family’s quasipolynomial decoder upper bound is outside the selected formalized statement.

problems.name: Arithmetic progressions
problems.assumptions: A nonconstant k-term arithmetic progression with fixed k ≥ 3, and subsets of {1,…,N}. The positive constants and decay exponent depend on k; changing k changes the comparison.
problems.formalizationScope: The reported Lean statement is the divergent-reciprocal-sum consequence. The quantitative progression-free-set upper bound displayed here is outside that selected statement.

problems.name: Van der Waerden numbers
problems.assumptions: For every integer colour count r ≥ 2 and all sufficiently large progression lengths k, with one absolute threshold independent of r. Wᵣ(k) is the least interval length forcing a monochromatic k-term progression.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes report the uniform lower bound with c = 1/100000, its growth limits, and boundary values. Sharper intermediate estimates are excluded. The catalogue headline itself states only c > 0.

problems.name: Planar unit distances
problems.assumptions: Unordered unit-distance pairs among n distinct points in the Euclidean plane. The exponent saving and multiplicative constant are absolute; this bound is distinct from the pinned-distances theorem.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes separately report a unit-distance bound with one fixed exponent β < 4/3 and a weak pinned-distances theorem. Neither description gives a numerical saving δ to rank.

problems.name: Halving lines
problems.assumptions: Even planar point sets with no three collinear, all sufficiently large sizes, and one absolute positive saving. A halving pair’s line leaves equally many remaining points on either side.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes report halving-pair bounds and level-switch bounds with additional generic-position assumptions. The constants are existential, rather than numerical headline values.

problems.name: Polynomial-free differences
problems.assumptions: A fixed intersective integer polynomial h of degree k ≥ 2 with positive leading coefficient. Differences exclude nonzero positive-argument values; intersective means a root modulo every modulus. Prime-argument variants require a stronger modular condition.
problems.formalizationScope: The reported Lean statement is the square-difference case. The general intersective-polynomial and prime-argument claims in the family description have broader scope.

problems.name: Thin spanning trees
problems.assumptions: Finite loopless k-edge-connected multigraphs with at least two vertices. Cuts count parallel edges with multiplicity, and the constructive runtime uses binary input length.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes report both an existential thin-tree bound and a separate deterministic polynomial-time construction. No numerical universal constant C is supplied.

problems.name: Quantum-state approximations
problems.assumptions: Unique ground states on open L×L squares, uniformly gapped nearest-neighbour Hamiltonians, bounded interactions, and global vector approximation error at most L⁻¹. Polynomial bond dimension is not a guarantee for arbitrary quantum states.
problems.formalizationScope: The catalogue does not list an accompanying top-line Lean formalization for this quantum-state approximation claim.

problems.name: Entangled-game repetition
problems.assumptions: A finite two-player one-round game with finite-dimensional entangled value v < 1, a fixed gap 0 < δ < 1−v, and independent repetitions. Joint entangled strategies and correlated questions within each game are allowed.
problems.formalizationScope: The notes report exponential decay with explicit dependence on δ and answer-set sizes. The separate distribution-dependent cubic bound is excluded; rates for different games or gaps are not directly comparable.
